doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: Photo session: wagons, parades and goodbyes
title: Mardi Gras parade photo and the saxophonist Vizcaro
summary: They look at a Canal and Royal Mardi Gras parade photo with Snyder, Nunez and Johnny Boyd, dated before 1911, and Laine tells of Vizcaro on saxophone.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: No. Do you remember anybody else on this big parade?
You remember anybody else on that parade? The Mardi Gras parade. That Mardi Gras parade. Let me see. Let me try it.
Let me see if I can see. I lost my good specs, mind you. Saturday evening. Oh, my. My good one, Saturday evening.
Yeah. I know you, and didn't you have Snyder playing bass drum with you?
Oh, yeah. That's Snyder. He's Jack.
And that's you here. Oh, Jack is on Snyder drum. Yeah.
Johnny Boyd. With his back there between the drums. And Snyder on bass drum then. That's the one. Yeah, Snyder on bass drum.
Yeah.
I have a little copy of that in a book.
You see, this looks like Nunes here.
Way over.
Right here. Down here. Facing the camera in the other group. That looks like Nunes. That's Yala? That looks like Yala, yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
Is that one of the coaches?
No. I don't believe that's one of the coaches. That ain't coach, but I don't know who that is. But that's some of your musicians. Where are you at? A lot of them. I know Snyder.
I have that Mexican from the what's-in-the-name band used to play at the West End on a saxophone in this band, too. I remember that. That's on Canal and Royal.
About what year is that, Jack?
Huh?
About what year?
Oh, brother, search me.

Did you have more than one band? I mean, would you have had another band? Yes, yes, yes, yes. The little booklet I have, the Southern Railroad, or somebody put this out in a book about 1911 with that picture. So I have a copy of that. I think it's at least 1911, then, or before. Oh, this before 1911? Yeah, before 1911.

Yes. Yes. Before 1911, then. Vizcaro was a fellow, that Mexican band was at West End. A Mexican called Vizcaro. He quit the Mexican band. He had some relation here, and he stayed here. He played a beautiful saxophone. Beautiful. I picked him up, too. A good reader. That's why I took him.
